examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

Влюбиться в + acc. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall in love', paired with 'влюбляться'.

examples.trans: That means you will fall in love soon.

meanings.note: Проводить время = to spend time. Common neuter noun meaning 'time' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

встать.gloss: to stand up, to get up

meanings.en: to stand up, to get up (out of bed)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stand up, to get up', paired with 'вставать'.

examples.text: Кто первый встал, того и тапки.
examples.trans: First come, first served (whoever got up first gets the slippers).

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: a brave person; also the main character of a story

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.

meanings.note: An idiom for a big telling-off. Common feminine noun meaning 'head' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Mum will tear my head off.

examples.text: Какая тебе опергруппа? Мне твоя мать голову оторвёт.
examples.trans: What field team? Your mother will tear my head off.

meanings.note: Head of a Russian region. From Latin 'gubernator' (helmsman, governor, borrowed from Greek 'kybernetes').

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Давление? Ничего, от тебя у меня просто кружится голова.
examples.trans: Blood pressure? It's nothing, you just make my head spin.

meanings.note: Also 'girlfriend' (моя девушка). Common feminine noun meaning 'young woman; girlfriend' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: For or belonging to children. Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('children's, childish').

examples.text: Мучить? Детские слова какие. Ну давай, мучай, Самсон!
examples.trans: Torture? What childish words. Go on then, torture me, Samson!

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

meanings.note: Стоять на коленях = to kneel. Common neuter noun meaning 'knee' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to steal', paired with 'украсть'.

Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give (away), to hand over', paired with 'отдавать'.

Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept', paired with 'принимать'.

examples.text: Ура, работает приёмчик! Это меня губернатор научил.

meanings.note: Locative в саду. Common masculine noun meaning 'garden, public park' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сейчас через сад и мост — и дома.
examples.trans: Right now through the park and the bridge, and I'm home.
The children are walking in the town park.

examples.text: Да вот иду уже! Сейчас через сад и мост — и дома.
examples.trans: I'm walking already! Right now through the park and the bridge, and I'm home.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Смотреть на + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

TV, a film. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to film, to take a photo/video of
meanings.note: Снять на телефон. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to film, to photograph; to take off; to rent', paired with 'снимать'.

Clothing. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to film, to photograph; to take off; to rent', paired with 'снимать'.

A flat or room. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to film, to photograph; to take off; to rent', paired with 'снимать'.

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон.
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone.
He took off his coat by the door.

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон. И сразу все мне помогают!
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone. And right away everyone helps me!

meanings.note: almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: Elderly man. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тарик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'old man' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This old man is sitting on the bench.
The old man told an interesting story.

examples.text: Я не могу спать спокойно! Этот старик крадёт у девушки лучшие годы.
examples.trans: I cannot sleep in peace! This old man is stealing the girl's best years.

meanings.note: Core Russian interj meaning 'stop!, cut!' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Stop, you cannot go any further!
Stop, that's a wrap! Good job, Samson!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pill, tablet' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Марина, иди ко мне! Я сегодня принял одну таблетку.
examples.trans: Marina, come to me! I took a pill today.

examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
